summary:
GET /api/files/:fileVersionId/download (file:// streaming branch) passed the stored choros.file_version.mime_type straight into res.setHeader('Content-Type', contentType). Node's http.ServerResponse.setHeader synchronously throws ERR_INVALID_CHAR if the value contains a control byte (\x00-\x1f, \x7f) — verified live: setHeader('Content-Type','text/plain\x00evil') throws 'Invalid character in header content'. The handler did not catch this; it propagates through withAuth into router.ts's generic catch, which maps any non-HttpError throw to sendErrorEnvelope(res,500,'INTERNAL',...). Today's only HTTP writer (POST /api/records/:recordId/files) already normalizes Content-Type from the request header before storing (rawCt.split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase()), so this path isn't reachable through it — but core/file-attachment.ts::addVersion accepts attrs.mime as an arbitrary string with no byte-level validation (only an optional mimeAllowlist, unset for most callers), so a secondary writer (document-render.ts today; any future seed/import/migration path) could still store a mime with a control byte, crashing every download of that version with a 500 instead of serving the file.

FIX: new sanitizeContentType(mime) in src/http/files.ts, applying the same read-time-boundary discipline T-0579's isInlineSafeMime already established (never trust only the writer, re-validate on read). It returns the mime unchanged if it's a non-empty string, under 4096 chars, and free of control bytes (regex /[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/); otherwise it returns 'application/octet-stream' (an existing structural default literal, not a new one). The download route now computes contentType = sanitizeContentType(rawMime) before setHeader, and additionally forces Content-Disposition: attachment (ignoring ?disposition=inline) whenever sanitization actually replaced the value — defense-in-depth so a mime that couldn't even survive being a valid HTTP header value can never ride the T-0579 inline allowlist path, independent of what that allowlist contains. Every mime that was already valid (text/plain, image/png, application/pdf, image/svg+xml, parameterized variants, etc.) passes through completely unchanged — this is purely an additive guard on a previously-uncaught-throw path, not a behavior change for any valid input.
test_proof_of_fix: src/__tests__/files-http.test.ts, new describe 'GET /api/files/:fileVersionId/download — Content-Type sanitization (T-0618)', 6 new tests: (1) AC-1 mimeType='text/plain\x00evil' → 200 (not 500), Content-Type: application/octet-stream, Content-Disposition: attachment, correct bytes streamed; (2) AC-1 CRLF header-injection attempt ('text/plain\r\nX-Injected: 1') → 200 octet-stream, no injected header present in the response; (3) AC-3 XSS-regression: 'text/html\x00' with ?disposition=inline → STILL attachment + octet-stream (control-byte mime never rides the inline path even though the payload written to the temp file is <script>alert(1)</script>); (4) AC-2 regression: 'text/plain' unaffected (passthrough); (5) AC-2 regression: 'image/png' + ?disposition=inline still inlines (allowlist behavior for valid mimes untouched); (6) AC-4: 5000+ char mime → 200 octet-stream (length guard).

ADVERSARIAL RE-VERIFY (manual): reverted sanitizeContentType call (git stash the fix, keep tests) — the new control-byte tests fail with the exact predicted symptom (500/ERR_INVALID_CHAR surfaced as a 500 through the router), confirming the tests are not tautological. Fix restored, all green again.

Full regression: all 54 tests in files-http.test.ts pass, including every pre-existing T-0579 inline-allowlist test (AC-11 series, B1/B1-residual svg-variant/param-stripping cases) — sanitization does not alter the existing XSS-gate behavior for any previously-covered mime.
sanitize_approach: sanitizeContentType(mime): non-empty string, length <= 4096, and free of any byte in [\x00-\x1f\x7f] (Node's HTTP header-invalid range) passes through unchanged; anything else (null/undefined/empty/control-byte-containing/too-long) becomes 'application/octet-stream'. Applied at the read-time boundary in the download route (same principle as isInlineSafeMime, T-0579) — not at the write boundary, since the goal is defense against ANY writer, present or future, not just the ones we control today.
tests_added: src/__tests__/files-http.test.ts: 6 new tests under 'GET /api/files/:fileVersionId/download — Content-Type sanitization (T-0618)' — control-byte NUL, CRLF-injection attempt, XSS-regression with html-ish control-byte mime + inline param, valid-mime passthrough (text/plain), valid inline-safe passthrough (image/png + inline), and an over-length-mime guard test.
